name: ASDS Droneship / Landing Zone
summary: Autonomous Spaceport Drone Ship (ASOG East Coast, OCISLY West Coast; JRTI repurposed early 2026) or concrete RTLS Landing Zone (active LZ-40 at CCSFS, active LZ-4 at VSFB; historical LZ-1 retired Aug 1, 2025).
function: Provides a stabilized ocean landing deck hundreds of kilometers downrange (ASDS) or a coastal concrete pad (RTLS) for propulsive first-stage booster recovery.
materials: Modified ocean-going steel deck barge (Marmac 300-series) equipped with four GPS-guided azimuth thrusters, blast walls, and the Octagrabber recovery robot.

specs.label: Active East Coast RTLS (LZ-40)
specs.source: CCSFS SLC-40 adjacent landing pad (replaced retired LZ-1)

specs.label: Historical LZ-1 (Retired Aug 2025)
specs.source: CCSFS former LC-13 (55 attempts, 54 successes; retired Aug 1, 2025 after Crew-11)

specs.label: Active West Coast RTLS (LZ-4)
specs.source: VSFB former SLC-4W (active since SAOCOM 1A, Oct 8, 2018)

history: SpaceX achieved its first RTLS landing at LZ-1 on Orbcomm-2 (Dec 2015) and its first ASDS ocean landing on OCISLY during CRS-8 (April 2016). LZ-1 retired on August 1, 2025 after Crew-11 when USSF reallocated LC-13, with East Coast RTLS operations shifting to LZ-40 adjacent to SLC-40. JRTI retired from Falcon 9 ASDS duties in early 2026 to support Starship transport, leaving ASOG (Port Canaveral) and OCISLY (Port of Long Beach) as the active Falcon 9 droneships.
sources: SpaceX Autonomous Spaceport Drone Ship Public Specs
